title: Online Planning for Sparse Ground Target Search from a High-Altitude UAV under Partial Observability

problem.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) searching for ground targets from a high altitude face a unique challenge, particularly when the target is already within the field of view but effectively unobservable because of its small apparent scale.
statements: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) searching for ground targets from a high altitude face a unique challenge, particularly when the target is already within the field of view but effectively unobservable because of its small apparent scale.
Standard object detectors often underperform in such scenarios because of resolution downscaling and limited context.
In contrast, active object search frameworks address this challenge by directing the agent to a suitable pose to gather richer visual information.

deploymentClaims: In the meantime, feature integration theory [21] highlighted that search time for an object increases linearly with the number of distractors (background objects possessing at least one feature with the object), which is explained by the sequential nature of attention deployment.

This theory was further refined with the guided search model [22], [23], which suggested that the order of sequential attention deployment is determined by the saliency of the attention map and the search time is more influenced by the signal-to-noise ratio rather than the number of distractors.
